Memo submitted. Summary of what I found:

**Three US expense lines exceeded both thresholds (>10% and >$5,000):**

| Acct | Line | Feb | Mar | Δ$ | Δ% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5000 | Hosting & Infrastructure | 31,301.80 | 40,948.20 | +9,646.40 | +30.8% |
| 6300 | Travel | 785.40 | 7,158.41 | +6,373.01 | +811% |
| 6400 | Marketing Programs | 7,898.14 | 29,686.00 | +21,787.86 | +276% |

**Hosting (5000) — explained at the ledger level.** The recurring Stackline production invoice is flat (STA-12523 $31,301.80 in Feb vs. STA-98877 $31,148.20 in Mar). The entire increase is JE-00258, a $9,800 "one-time data migration" invoice (SC-M-2203). One caution: the invoice number doesn't follow the vendor's usual STA-##### series, and I wasn't able to open the document itself, so I've asked that it be reviewed for period and authenticity before this driver is accepted.

**Travel (6300) and Marketing (6400) — drivers do NOT hold up yet.** I hit the tool-call budget before the March Travel detail and the Feb/Mar Marketing detail returned. February Travel was four small card charges ($785 total); a ~9x jump with Training & Conferences simultaneously dropping to zero suggests possible miscoding. Marketing's +$21.8k is the largest single item and is unexplained until tied to specific invoices. Both are called out in the memo as open flux items.

**Below-threshold but worth your attention:** March depreciation (6800) and bank fees (6900) are both $0 versus $3,425 and $65 in February — these look like missing close entries rather than real movements.

I posted no entries and made no formal exception flags, since the budget ran out before I could get the supporting detail; the memo lists the specific follow-ups needed.
